prize_parts.citation: For the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, based on magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from B035 to B008. The optical lattice clock is a single, sharply defined invention: Katori's magic-wavelength condition makes the trapping potential invisible to the clock transition, so Doppler and recoil shifts vanish while very many atoms are interrogated at once, and Ye's group took this to about 1e-18 and into many-body clock physics. The performance is reproduced in Sr, Yb and Hg in several independent laboratories, and the Katori and Ye pairing maps cleanly onto proposal and first demonstration versus record accuracy. I still regard its weight as lying in measurement capability more than in a new understanding of matter, but relativistic geodesy and sensitivity to variations of constants are real physics uses, and the round-1 exchange shows that the two points that held B035 back for me are not answered by the citation.
statement.case_against: My main reservation about B008 is unchanged in kind: it is adjacent to the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and a two-name credit leaves out NIST, PTB, SYRTE, Tokyo and ion-clock groups, plus the pending SI second redefinition. These can be met only by a narrow citation on the lattice concept. For B035, the case I still find scientifically most original, the problems are that the credited trio cannot include Yuan Cao without exceeding the three-name limit, and that the origin of the correlated states is still being argued.

responses.point: Johansson holds that the debated origin of superconductivity and the missing experimental credit for Cao, Fatemi, Dean and Young are reasons to prefer a result with a settled interpretation.
responses.response: I accept the attribution half of this fully. In round 1 I treated the Cao omission as a footnote, but with a three-name ceiling it is structural: the decisive 2018 devices were made and measured largely by Cao, and any trio that credits the group leader without him is exposed. I still do not think an unsettled mechanism disqualifies a discovery, since the flat bands and the correlated insulators are reproduced, but the two problems together are enough that I would not stake the 2026 prize on B035.

responses.point: Kroll argues that precedent does not weaken B008 because the 2005 prize rewarded comb-based frequency measurement while the lattice clock is a different idea about how to trap and interrogate the atoms, and that the citation should stay on the lattice concept.
responses.response: That is persuasive and it answers the chair's first question as far as I can judge from outside the field. The comb is a ruler for optical frequencies and the 2012 ion work concerns control of one quantum system, whereas the magic-wavelength lattice solves a different problem, the combination of many atoms and no first-order trapping shift. I therefore drop my concern about overlap to a drafting issue. I also note your disclosed laboratory proximity to this area, and I would suggest it be discounted, not that it changes the physics.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers the trapped-ion line B022 as stable for decades, but concedes that Blatt's experimental share is contestable because of Wineland's NIST group and Monroe, and that part of the foundation was honoured in 2012.
responses.response: I agree that the proposal-plus-experiment structure is attractive, but the same overlap with the 2012 prize that you raise against your own case is stronger here than for the clock, and the Blatt allocation is a judgment call that several members press. For those reasons B022 does not enter my configuration, and I would put it behind B008 and B035 in my alternatives, within the two-alternative limit.

responses.point: Olsson says the credit gap for Cao is not minor and that a B035 citation would have to describe flat bands and correlated phases rather than a mechanism, so she prefers to wait.
responses.response: I now agree with the waiting argument more than I did. On your point about the citation, drafting narrowly is possible, but narrow wording cannot repair the missing experimentalist. Waiting also costs little, because the field is progressing and a better settled configuration may exist in a few years. I keep B035 as my first alternative so that it stays visible, and I keep B009 as the second, acknowledging your disclosed proximity to it.

uncertainties: Whether the priority between Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and the first lattice-clock demonstrations, and the contributions of other groups, is fully captured by the two names.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for the SI second redefinition, and whether that timing argument cuts for or against a prize in 2026.
Whether the weight I give to B008 as a precision measurement rather than a change in understanding of matter will be shared by the other members who regard the fundamental-physics uses as decisive.
statement.conflict_note: No documented tie to Katori, Ye or the other credited people for B008, B035 or B009 appears in my profile. My field of electronic-structure and 2D-materials theory is adjacent to B035, and I continue to discount that, particularly as I have now moved away from it. Having chaired the 2025 cycle, I weigh the circuit QED case (B012) with some caution because of its closeness to that prize.
